_comment: L1 plan Task 16 (docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-14-l1-curated-library.md): J. S. Bach's Little Preludes, the Applicatio and six Two-Part Inventions, engraved by the Mutopia Project. Facts from content/tools/candidates.json and the fetched RDF; retrievedAt is the fetch log's date. Fields as documented in catalog.json's _comment. Syllabus anchors: Henle's per-piece levels (https://www.henle.de/Little-Preludes-and-Fughettas/HN-106, https://www.henle.de/Two-Part-Inventions/HN-1591; Henle 2 is about our 3, Henle 3 about our 4, Henle 4 about our 5) and the RCM Piano Syllabus 2022 (https://teacherportal.rcmusic.com/getattachment/57f3734d-97e5-4777-b67e-4b1111ee31a3/piano-syllabus-2022-edition.pdf; List A, RCM 3 to 5 is about our 3, 6 to 7 about our 4, 8 to 9 about our 5).

pieces.title: Little Prelude in C major (Clavier-Büchlein for W. F. Bach)
pieces.tempoSource: editorial: the source prints no tempo and its \midi block sets none (LilyPond's default 60); quarter = 72 keeps the running sixteenths at about 5 notes a second, as in the core Invention No. 1 (quarter = 80)
pieces.levelNote: Level 3: Henle HN 106 level 2 'easy' (about our 3); not in the RCM 2022 syllabus; heuristic proposes 3 (score 5.41)
pieces.notes: From the Clavier-Büchlein vor Wilhelm Friedemann Bach (begun 1720). Mutopia title '9 Little Preludes - 1 - C Major'. Engraved by JD Erickson from the Bach-Gesellschaft edition (1853). The engraving is CC BY-SA 3.0 (attribution: JD Erickson / Mutopia Project); this MusicXML is shared under the same license. The converter has no MusicXML mapping for LilyPond's \upmordent (bass, bars 3 and 5) and \downmordent (bass, bar 4): a catalog patch writes them as \prallmordent, which it exports as a long mordent (<mordent long="yes"/>), as it already treats \upprall and \downprall; the approach from below or above is not kept.

pieces.title: Little Prelude in D minor (Five Little Preludes, No. 2)
pieces.tempoSource: editorial: the source prints no tempo and its \midi block sets none (LilyPond's default 60); quarter = 60 kept deliberately, a calm pulse for the dotted figures, held suspensions and sixteenth turns
pieces.levelNote: Level 4: Henle HN 106 level 3 'easy', about our 4 (the plan's table had 3); not in the RCM 2022 syllabus; heuristic proposes 3 (score 5.19); borderline 3/4, only 10 bars
pieces.notes: No. 2 of the Five Little Preludes (Fünf kleine Präludien, BWV 939-943). Mutopia title 'Praeludium Nr. 2'. The source declares the signature as \key f \major; the piece is in D minor. Engraved by Hajo Dezelski from the Bach-Gesellschaft edition, vol. 36 (ed. Ernst Naumann, 1890). The engraving is CC BY-SA 3.0 (attribution: Hajo Dezelski / Mutopia Project); this MusicXML is shared under the same license. The published Mutopia MIDI (LilyPond 2.11) has 168 of the 169 notes: in bar 5 an E4 sixteenth re-strikes (beat 3, last sixteenth) while another upper-staff voice holds the same E4, and the old MIDI writer dropped the overlapping re-attack (the same case as M0's Moonlight). LilyPond 2.24's MIDI of the same source matches all 169.

pieces.title: Applicatio in C major
pieces.tempoSource: LilyPond \midi block of the source (tempoWholesPerMinute 85/4, quarter = 85); no printed tempo mark. Plausible: a moderate pulse for eighths with ornaments
pieces.levelNote: Level 3: no published placement found (not listed by Henle HN 106 or the RCM 2022 syllabus); the opening lesson of the Clavier-Büchlein, 8 bars with ornaments and some three-voice writing; heuristic proposes 3 (score 5.01)
pieces.notes: The first piece of the Clavier-Büchlein vor Wilhelm Friedemann Bach (1720), a fingering lesson: Bach's manuscript carries his own fingerings. This engraving reproduces the Bach-Gesellschaft text without them, so there is no editorial-fingering copy. Engraved by Allen Garvin and placed in the public domain. Both halves repeat (written once, with repeat signs).

pieces.title: Invention No. 4 in D minor
pieces.tempoSource: LilyPond \midi block of the source (tempoWholesPerMinute 90/4, quarter = 90, dotted quarter = 60); no printed tempo mark. Plausible: one beat a bar, sixteenths at 6 notes a second
pieces.levelNote: Level 4: Henle HN 1591 level 3 'easy' and RCM 2022 Level 7 List A, both about our 4, like the core Invention No. 1; heuristic proposes 3 (score 5.67), which underrates counterpoint
pieces.notes: Engraved by Allen Garvin from the Bach-Gesellschaft edition and placed in the public domain. The source sets LilyPond 1.x's old-relative option, which convert-ly 2.24 refuses; the line is removed before conversion (a catalog patch). It changes nothing here: old-relative only affects a note that follows a chord inside relative mode, and this piece has no chords. The published Mutopia MIDI, rendered from the unpatched source, confirms the pitches.
